basis: Defined by hemorrhage into skin or mucosa; classified as a hematologic hemorrhagic disorder.
Defining limb and vertebral dysplasia; gingival overgrowth and structural tongue/dental abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Facial appearance alone does not establish ocular damage.
Nutritional choline deficiency; fatty liver and hepatocellular injury are common (>30% in depletion studies). The supplied cirrhosis evidence concerns animals.
Inherited basal ganglia and other cerebral calcification with neurologic dysfunction; localized cerebral vessel calcification does not establish systemic vascular disease.
Inherited corneal epithelial dystrophy causing recurrent erosions and visual symptoms.
Ovarian endocrine overstimulation with defining vascular permeability dysfunction; pleural effusions occur in 30-79%. Renal failure and pulmonary edema are minority complications.
Aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease comprises immune-mediated airway inflammation, asthma and nasal polyposis.
Colonic/duodenal polyposis; intellectual disability and epidermoid cysts/early balding each occur in 30-79%. Retinal pigment hypertrophy usually does not impair vision; anemia is secondary.
The definition explicitly locates this benign vascular neoplasm in scrotal skin.
Defining severe skeletal dysplasia; night blindness and gingival overgrowth each occur in 80-99%. Ear shape and extramedullary hematopoiesis alone do not establish functional damage.
Glycosylation disorder with defining neurologic and visual impairment; dermatitis 5/7, ichthyosis 4/7. Common liver enzyme abnormalities, anemia and coagulation defects omitted by cap.
Axonal peripheral sensorimotor neuropathy; persistent denervation-related muscle wasting is documented in 20/20 patients.
MAN1B1 glycosylation disorder with defining intellectual disability; cutis laxa 5/7 and strabismus 5/12. Joint hypermobility 7/19 omitted by cap.
Psychotic and mood disorder without defining damage to an included organ axis.
Inherited alteration of a CD4 T-cell surface epitope; altered antibody recognition does not itself establish functional immunodeficiency.
Benign bone-forming neoplasm arising in bone, often the vertebrae; spinal location alone does not imply nervous system damage.
Inherited macular retinal dystrophy causing central visual impairment.
Primordial skeletal growth disorder with defining microcephaly and intellectual disability; supplied dental and ocular abnormalities lack frequencies supporting additional involvement.
Bone fragility, fractures, radial head dislocation and interosseous membrane mineralization define this subtype; dentinogenesis imperfecta is explicitly absent.
Defined by cerebral small-vessel disease and ocular developmental defects. Renal disease and myopathy are concentrated in particular subtypes and are not established as common across the umbrella.
Degenerative cerebellar and pyramidal disorder; ocular dysmetria and supranuclear gaze palsy reflect central neurologic dysfunction.
Permanent beta-cell dysfunction defines the umbrella; neurologic, cardiac and skeletal defects cluster in syndromic subtypes. Diabetic retinopathy and nephropathy are separate diseases.
Purulent infection occupying the vitreous, supported by the abscess and infectious endophthalmitis ancestors.
UBTF-related neurodegeneration with regression, cerebral atrophy and extrapyramidal dysfunction; dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction without demonstrated gastrointestinal injury.
Defining neurodevelopmental regression; scoliosis occurs in 241/467 (~52%) and muscle atrophy in 30-79%. Disordered breathing is central; constipation alone does not establish organ damage.
